title: arXiv might not survive AI slop onslaught, warn mathematicians
source_used: none for the article itself (New Scientist page refused; no other outlet carries it); context on arXiv's earlier cap read on The Register
why_it_matters_hint: From the headline only: mathematicians warn that arXiv, where researchers post papers before peer review, might not survive a flood of AI-generated low-quality submissions.
event_date: Article dated 5 Oct 2026 (Google News 17:38 GMT); arXiv's two-a-month cap, the earlier story, was announced on Thursday 1 Oct 2026 (The Register, 2 Oct 2026).
notes: The New Scientist page returned HTTP 406 and its public feed also refused; Google News searches on 6 Oct 2026 found no other outlet carrying this piece, so no article text was obtained and the entry rests on the headline. Context read in full on The Register ('ArXiv imposes rate limit on paper submissions to stem the AI slop tide', 2 Oct 2026): arXiv limits each submitter to two new submissions per calendar month, with three active submissions at a time, announced on Thursday 1 Oct 2026 by community engagement manager Kat Boboris and effective immediately, after 40,363 submissions in September 2026 against 9,869 in September 2016 and 20,569 two years ago; arXiv calls the cap a stopgap while it works out new practices. The pool marks this item as a follow-up of the 2 Oct 2026 item 'arXiv now limits every researcher to two paper submissions a month' (Startup Fortune); no edition of ours since 23 Sep carried the cap.
